newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-LEHMAN WINS GOLF WRITERS' AWARD.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-LEHMAN WINS GOLF WRITERS' AWARD.

text.p: Tom Lehman was voted the Golf Writers Association of America's Player of the Year and Britain's Laura Davies was the Female Player of the Year, the organisation announced on Monday.
Lehman, winner of the British Open and one-stroke runnerup in the U.S. Open, received 187 votes. Rookie professional Tiger Woods was a distant second with 20 votes and Phil Mickelson third with nine.

The women's vote was closer, with non-U.S. players the top three. Davies received 79 votes to win for the second time in three years while Australian rookie Karrie Webb got 51 and Sweden's Annika Sorenstam, last year's winner, 43. Dottie Pepper got four votes and Betsy King one.
Jim Colbert repeated as Senior Player of the Year. He received 84 votes, Hale Irwin 77 and John Bland 11.
Lehman, 37, had 13 top 10 finishes in 22 starts and a six-shot victory in the PGA Tour Championship contested by the year's 30 leading money winners.
The Minnesotan led the PGA Tour this year in official money with $1,780,159 and won the Vardon Trophy for scoring with an average of 69.32 strokes per round.
He wound up the year by winning the Mastercard Grand Slam's 36-hole event in Hawaii over Masters champion Nick Faldo, U.S. Open winner Steve Jones and PGA champion Mark Brooks.

Davies, 31, won four events including two women's majors -- the McDonald's LPGA Championship and the du Maurier Classic. She also reaped the season's biggest payday, $340,000 in the LPGA Skins Game, although it did not count on the official money list.
Davies won the scoring championship with a 70.32 average and had 13 top 10 finishes while collecting $927,302 in official earnings.

Webb, 21, started her first LPGA season with two second-place finishes and one first-place in her first three events. She finished with three tournament titles, capping the year by winning the Tour Championship by four shots and becoming the first LPGA player to break the million dollar mark in one season with $1,002,000 in 24 starts.
Sorenstam, who also won three events, repeated as U.S. Open champion and had a 70.47 scoring average, second only to Davies.
